title: Andrew Ng: Building Faster with AI
summary: Andrew Ng at YC Startup School: speed as the key to startups, AI's much bigger boost for prototypes than production code, product management as the new bottleneck, and why everyone should learn to code.

assertions.quote: maybe 10 times faster ... for production code ... maybe 30 to 50% faster

verdicts.note: Direction is well supported: greenfield, low-stakes work gets the biggest gains in studies and surveys. The specific multipliers are anecdote.
Time-to-prototype gains are the most common reported outcome (45% of sources), while production use is weakly evidenced. The gap is consistent with the claim but not quantified.

assertions.quote: I've rebuilt a codebase three times in the last month

verdicts.note: True for small, well-tested components and test suites; for large systems with implicit behavior, rewrites still lose knowledge and introduce regressions.

assertions.quote: some people are telling people not to learn to code ... it'll go down as some of the worst career advice ever

verdicts.note: Basic coding helps people direct and check AI output, and adoption among non-engineers is growing. The labor-market payoff for non-engineers is still unproven.

assertions.quote: I've heard teams start to propose PM to engineering ratio of one to 0.5

verdicts.note: Consistent with Amdahl-style reasoning and reports of shifting PM:engineer ratios; evidence is mostly anecdotal from AI-native teams.

assertions.quote: being half a generation behind makes a big difference

verdicts.note: Tool-use and long-horizon capability jumps in 2025 changed effective workflows (chat-with-RAG to agentic loops); consistent with practitioner reports.

assertions.quote: hype narratives ... that make these businesses look more powerful ... helpful for raising money

verdicts.note: Labs do have incentives and many evals are self-reported, but independent evals (METR, SWE-bench, LMArena) largely confirm capability gains.

assertions.quote: people that know how to use AI will replace people that don't

verdicts.note: A slogan about future labor competition, not a testable claim; plausible but unmeasured.
